correctness.rationale: For every real a in [7/10,4/5], exact quadratic Bernstein coefficients certify V_a'(1/2)>0, V_a'(3/5)<0, V_a'(3/4)>0 and V_a'(9/10)<0. The derivative polynomial has exactly three sign changes and thus at most three positive roots; IVT provides three, hence exactly two maxima separated by a minimum. On the explicit fully bifurcating ultrametric ten-tip tree, the strict rational derivative margins are proved by expansion of the edge-covariance formula and independently checked by exact survivor-set enumeration. The proof is uniform; finite enumeration is not used for the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: Faller–Pardi–Steel (2008) already contains the general variance covariance identity, but their full text Lemma 2.1 and theorem/conclusion were inspected and do not classify the number of stationary points of variance as a common extinction probability changes. The present work establishes exactly three critical points over a continuous interval of tree shapes, and nonunimodality on a fully resolved binary tree, not merely a new evaluation of their formula. O'Dwyer et al. and Nipperess–Matsen likewise cover mean/variance for other sampling formulations without the interval-wide modal theorem.
residual_risks: General variance identities already imply algorithmic evaluation of any fixed tree, so originality is restricted to the explicit interval-wide qualitative modal theorem and strictly binary persistence.
The supplemental variance derivation in doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002832 could not be fully read; no modal theorem was seen in its main text.
Unindexed papers might contain a stronger general theorem about variance as a function of equal survival probability; absence of a search hit is not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The risk-dependent variability of future biodiversity, unlike its monotone mean, can exhibit two separated uncertainty peaks. This is a structurally meaningful boundary for evaluating approximation and uncertainty assumptions under homogeneous independent extinction; it holds on a continuum of positive branch lengths and even strictly bifurcating ultrametric trees. The result is not asserted to be minimal, empirically common, or an all-tree classification.
